why: The product itself: when the board is built, where its link lives, and how a comment sent from it becomes a fix, a push and a reply. Every other file serves this procedure.
The payload contract between the collector and the page: every revision of every file, blobs deduplicated. Changing it later means rebuilding every published board.
The revision model: a file's history is its first-parent commits on the branch, renames followed by asking for both paths. Every range a reviewer can pick comes from here.
Which diff a file shows: the board's range, the reviewer's own, or the agent's shift, newest wins. Viewed is tied to the blob shown, so a new change unmarks it.
Where state lives: the reviewer's marks private in the artifact's db, the agent's shifts shared and read-only, and a board that keeps working with no db at all.
The anchor grammar a comment carries back to the agent — path, commit range, side, line or line span, within 128 bytes. It is the one format that outlives the page.

The board takes over the claude.ai shell's comment mode: a click comments instead of acting, and resolves to a line, a file, or the control under it. This is the riskiest bet — an undocumented contract with the host.
Dragging in comment mode: across rows it becomes a line-span comment, elsewhere a drawn rectangle. Pointer handling in the capture phase decides what the rest of the board still receives.
This file's own reader: what an agent may mark, and why a bad path or span fails the build rather than drawing nothing.
Looks like lint plumbing, but it is the architecture: it decides which layer and app may import which, so every later artifact app is shaped by it.
